slots.practicalActivity: Write a real bash script that starts with #!/usr/bin/env bash and set -euo pipefail, quotes every variable expansion, checks a condition before acting (e.g. a directory existing) and exits 1 with a message on stderr if it doesn't, and uses trap to guarantee a lock file is removed on exit no matter how the script ends.
slots.deliverable: A saved .sh script using set -euo pipefail, quoted variables, a meaningful nonzero exit code on failure, and a trap-based cleanup, run at least twice to prove the trap fires correctly.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a lib/common.sh with a log() function (timestamped, level-tagged) and a retry() function that retries a failing command N times with a delay, each using local for its variables; source lib/common.sh from two separate real scripts and confirm both use the exact same logging output.
slots.deliverable: A lib/common.sh file with log() and retry() functions, sourced successfully by at least two separate scripts that each produce matching timestamped log output.

slots.practicalActivity: Using a real log file on your machine (or a downloaded sample access log), write a one-line pipeline chaining grep -E, awk, sort, and uniq -c to produce a 'top 5' frequency report (e.g. top status codes or top requested paths), then use sed to redact one sensitive field (like an IP address) from a sample of the output.
slots.deliverable: A terminal transcript showing a working grep | awk | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -5 pipeline against a real log file, plus a sed redaction command and its output.

slots.practicalActivity: Schedule one of your own scripts from this chapter with crontab -e using a real cron line that redirects both stdout and stderr to a log file (>> logfile 2>&1), confirm it fires (a */1 * * * * test schedule works for verification), then kick off a second long-running command with nohup ... & disown and confirm with ps that it survives closing your terminal session.
slots.deliverable: A crontab entry that ran successfully at least once with output captured in a log file, plus a demonstrated nohup/disown job confirmed still running after the launching terminal closed.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review for Bash for Automation: combine everything so far into one script — set -euo pipefail, functions sourced from lib/common.sh, a real text-processing pipeline over a log file, and output redirected the way a cron job would need — and schedule it with crontab -e.
slots.deliverable: One combined bash script using safe-script habits, a shared library, and a text-processing pipeline, successfully scheduled and confirmed to have run via cron.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a Python script with a dictionary of at least 5 real hostnames (your own machines, VMs, or realistic made-up ones) mapped to a disk-usage percentage, loop over it with .items(), and print ALERT/WARNING/OK for each using if/elif/else against a threshold, then wrap the check in an is_over_threshold(usage, threshold=90) function with a default argument.
slots.deliverable: A runnable .py script that loops a dict of servers through a threshold check function and prints a correct ALERT/WARNING/OK line for each one.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a Python script using pathlib that rglobs a real directory on your machine for files matching a pattern (e.g. *.log or *.txt), reads one with a with-open block, writes a filtered copy of its contents to a new file, then uses shutil.move to relocate the original into a created archive/ subdirectory.
slots.deliverable: A .py script that finds real files with Path.rglob, filters and rewrites one with a with-block, and moves the original into an archive/ folder using shutil.move.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a Python script that runs a real external command (e.g. git status, or df -h) via subprocess.run with capture_output=True, text=True, and a timeout, checks result.returncode to decide success/failure, and prints result.stdout and result.stderr accordingly — using shell=False with a list of arguments throughout.
slots.deliverable: A .py script that runs a real command with subprocess.run, correctly branches on returncode, and includes a working timeout.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a real server-health.py CLI tool: argparse with a required positional host, an optional --threshold with a default, and a --verbose flag (store_true); wire in a logging setup with both a FileHandler and a StreamHandler at different levels, wrap the health check in try/except with a custom HealthCheckError, and return a meaningful sys.exit() code.
slots.deliverable: A working server-health.py accepting real CLI arguments (including --help), logging to both a file and the console, and exiting with a correct, documented exit code on success and failure.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review for Python for Automation: extend your server-health.py tool from the previous slot so it loops over a real list of 3+ hostnames, calls subprocess to run an actual local command against each (e.g. ping -c 1 or df -h via SSH if you have a second machine), and logs a pass/fail per host with the logging module instead of print().
slots.deliverable: An extended CLI tool that checks multiple real hosts via subprocess, with every result logged (not printed) to both a file and the console.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a sample nested JSON file by hand (an order with a destination object and an events array) and parse it with json.load, pulling a nested value safely with .get() and a default; then write an equivalent config as YAML with a mapping, a nested block, and a list, and load it with yaml.safe_load, confirming it produces the same dict/list shapes as the JSON version.
slots.deliverable: Two small scripts — one parsing a real nested JSON file, one parsing an equivalent YAML file with yaml.safe_load — both printing the same extracted values.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a real .env file with a fake API key, add it to .gitignore before ever touching git add, load it in a Python script with python-dotenv's load_dotenv() and read it via os.environ (not .get(), so a missing key fails loudly), then confirm with git status that .env never shows as trackable.
slots.deliverable: A .env file correctly git-ignored from first creation, loaded successfully into a script via load_dotenv() and os.environ, with git status confirming it is untracked.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a real Jinja2 template (e.g. an nginx-style config or a simple app-config.yaml.j2) with {{ }} placeholders, an {% if %} block, and a {% for %} loop over a list; render it three times with three different Python dicts (e.g. dev/staging/production) and write each rendered result to its own output file.
slots.deliverable: One Jinja2 template file and three distinct, correctly rendered output files generated from it by changing only the input data, not the template.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review for Data Formats & Configuration: write one Python script that reads a YAML config with yaml.safe_load, pulls a secret from an .env-loaded environment variable, renders a Jinja2 template using values from both, and writes the rendered result out as a JSON-logged summary with json.dumps(indent=2).
slots.deliverable: One script tying together YAML config loading, environment-variable secrets, and Jinja2 templating into a single rendered output file.

slots.practicalActivity: Call a real public REST API (e.g. a free weather, GitHub, or JSONPlaceholder API) with requests.get, passing real query parameters and a timeout, check the response with raise_for_status(), parse response.json(), then write a small loop that follows real pagination (or simulates it against a paginated endpoint) until no next page remains.
slots.deliverable: A .py script that successfully calls a real public API with parameters and a timeout, handles a non-200 response correctly, and collects results across at least 2 pages if the API paginates.

slots.practicalActivity: Using a real API that requires a key (e.g. a free-tier API like OpenWeatherMap or a GitHub personal access token against api.github.com), store the key in an environment variable, send it as a header (X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer), and confirm a call without the header is rejected while a call with it succeeds.
slots.deliverable: A script authenticating to a real API with a key read from an environment variable, with a captured failed call (no auth) and a captured successful call (with auth) for comparison.

slots.practicalActivity: Using a real free-tier cloud account (AWS, Azure, or GCP), authenticate a Python SDK client (e.g. boto3.client('ec2') or the Azure SDK equivalent), list a real resource type with a filter or paginator, and tag at least one real resource to mark it for review rather than deleting anything outright.
slots.deliverable: A script that authenticates to a real cloud account via its SDK, lists a filtered set of real resources, and successfully applies a tag to at least one of them.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a minimal Flask app with a /webhooks/test POST endpoint that verifies an HMAC signature (hmac.compare_digest against a shared secret in an environment variable) before trusting the payload, run it locally, and send it a real signed POST request with curl or Python's requests to confirm a correct signature is accepted and a tampered one is rejected with a 401.
slots.deliverable: A running local Flask webhook receiver with working HMAC signature verification, demonstrated accepting one correctly-signed request and rejecting one tampered request.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for APIs & Cloud Automation: chain this chapter together in one script that authenticates to a real API with a token from an environment variable, pulls paginated data from it, and writes a summary of what it found to a JSON file — the same shape of work the capstone's inventory-pull step will reuse.
slots.deliverable: One script authenticating with a real token, pulling paginated API data, and writing the summarized result to a JSON file.

slots.practicalActivity: Write an idempotent bash setup-user.sh that checks id -u before creating a user and grep -qF before appending an SSH key, run it twice to prove reruns are safe; then write a Python script using re with named capture groups and collections.Counter to parse a real or realistic log file and print a short failure-rate summary plus the top 3 failure reasons.
slots.deliverable: An idempotent setup-user.sh confirmed safe to run twice with identical results, plus a log-parsing script producing a Counter-based summary report from a real log file.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a bash script that backs up a real local file or small database export, compresses it with gzip, and enforces a retention policy in Python (delete anything older than N days with Path.glob and .stat().st_mtime); then write a health-check script combining a real HTTP endpoint check (requests with a timeout) and a local shutil.disk_usage check, alerting to a real Slack incoming webhook only when status changes.
slots.deliverable: A working backup-plus-retention script and a health-check script that posts a real alert to a Slack webhook on a status transition, demonstrated with at least one real alert received.

lessons.title: Capstone Kickoff: Automate a Repetitive Admin Workflow

slots.practicalActivity: Plan then build launch_store.py end to end: an argparse CLI (--store-id, --store-name, --region), a Jinja2-rendered per-store YAML config written to disk, a call to your idempotent user-setup script via subprocess, and a call to a real or realistic REST API (reusing Chapter 4's authenticated pattern) to pull a baseline and save it as JSON — with every step logged and the whole run wrapped in try/except.
slots.deliverable: A working launch_store.py that, given real CLI arguments, renders a config, runs the idempotent setup step, pulls and saves API data, and logs every step to a file.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Slack alert to launch_store.py reporting success or exactly which step failed, split the except block to distinguish a setup failure (RuntimeError) from an API failure (requests.exceptions.RequestException) with a different alert message for each, then write a README documenting the problem, usage, and design decisions, and run the finished tool once end to end with real arguments.
slots.deliverable: A completed launch_store.py with distinct failure-path alerts to a real Slack webhook, a written README, and one successful end-to-end run against real (or realistic practice) inputs.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can write production-habited Bash and Python scripts that parse and report on real logs, read and template real config files, call and authenticate to real REST APIs and cloud SDKs, and ship one complete automation tool that sets up a resource, logs every step, and alerts a team on success or failure.
